Continuing from pose (2.950, 7.400), heading 225, with 50 frames left, I'm thinking I need to translate to break the viewing degeneracy on that constant-x edge. Since the edge runs along y at fixed x, I need to shift my position in x or y to get proper parallax on its location.

The core issue is that from a single viewpoint, a straight edge only constrains a plane through the camera center and the observed image line — the edge could lie anywhere along that plane. Rotating in place doesn't move the camera center, so it can't resolve this; only translating to a genuinely different position gives a second plane whose intersection with the first pins down the actual 3D line.

Given my current position at (2.95, 7.40), the structure edge sits roughly at x≈0.70-1.34, y≈3.2-5.0. I'm considering moving west to (2.20, 7.40) since that's clear of the sofa (which spans x 2.19-3.11, y 5.67-6.8) and gets me closer with better parallax, then reorienting toward the structure's estimated center around (1.0, 4.1).

Working through the math: from (2.20, 7.40) heading west (270°), turning -70° gives heading 200° pointed at the structure. So the plan is two frames — turn +45°/move 0.75 to reach (2.20, 7.40) at h=270, then turn -70°/move 0 to face h=200 toward the structure. I'm also noting an unswept pocket north of the sofa around x 2.6-3.9, y 7.45-8.27 to revisit later.

Now I'm reconsidering coverage: from an earlier frame at (3.70,7.40) facing west, I saw the west/north walls, but I still need a vantage point for that small sofa-adjacent pocket, maybe standing near (2.95,7.40) and turning to face east (h=90) to capture the x>2.95 strip within the 90° FOV.

Since going from h=225 to h=90 requires more than one 90° turn, I'm mapping out cheaper turn sequences — maybe two steps through 135° or deferring this pocket to later.

With about 50 frames to spend, I'm prioritizing: first resolving the structure_1 ambiguity since that yields the highest information gain, then confirming sofa_1 against structure_1, then sweeping remaining unexplored areas.

But I want to reconsider whether structure_1 could actually be something else entirely — a large sofa, sectional, or bed sitting near the room's center rather than an ambiguous structural feature, since its gray blocky multi-toned appearance doesn't clearly rule that out.

If it were shadow on the floor, we'd see plant-colored pixels where the plant base is, not gray — so this must be an occluding object rather than a shadow. I'll move forward with the plan: execute f151, turning +45° from heading 225 to 270, then moving 0.75 units west along that new heading, and re-measure from there.
